entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lorenzo Ghiberti was an Italian Renaissance sculptor from Florence, a key figure in the Early Renaissance, best known as the creator of two sets of bronze doors of the Florence Baptistery, the later one called by Michelangelo the Gates of Paradise. Born in Florence around 1377, he was trained as a goldsmith and sculptor, establishing an important workshop for sculpture in metal. His book of Commentarii contains important writing on art, as well as what may be the earliest surviving autobiography by any artist.

Ghiberti's work in Florence was heavily influenced by the Medici family, who commissioned him to create the bronze doors in the 1420s. The doors, which were completed in 1450, featured intricate sculptures of biblical figures and became a symbol of the city's artistic and cultural rebirth.

Lorenzo Ghiberti's legacy extends beyond his own work, as he played a significant role in the development of Renaissance sculpture and art. His innovative use of bronze and his emphasis on technique and craftsmanship raised the bar for artists of his time, influencing generations to come.

Ghiberti's contributions to art history are still celebrated today, with his bronze doors remaining one of the most iconic works of the Renaissance. His legacy can be seen in the many artists who followed in his footsteps, including Michelangelo and Sandro Botticelli.

The bronze doors, which are now considered a masterpiece of Renaissance art, continue to inspire awe and wonder in visitors to the Florence Baptistery. They serve as a testament to Ghiberti's skill and artistry, and his place in the pantheon of Renaissance masters.
